final:
STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: One reproduced blocking bug: when a handler hijacks after writing a 200 (or after WriteHeader(200)), the middleware drops the status line and headers, so the client gets raw bytes with no HTTP response head. Everything else I probed held: gzip ordering, GetHead, ServeContent, ReadFrom, Flush, 1xx, late headers, panics, and -race concurrency. Probe files are deleted and git status matches the start.
FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files middleware/zz_probe_test.go and middleware/zz_probe2_test.go were created and deleted)
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Hijack after a buffered 200 loses the response head. Probe: handler calls `w.WriteHeader(200)` (or `w.Write`) then `http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()` and writes "RAW". Without the middleware the client receives `HTTP/1.1 200 OK | Date | Connection: close | Transfer-Encoding: chunked | | RAW`. With `r.Use(ETag)` the client receives only `RAW`. Cause: Hijack forwards to net/http without first sending the held snapshot head, and `hijacked` then suppresses `finish`. Fix: in Hijack, when `wroteHeader && !passthrough`, send the snapshot status and headers before hijacking, or document and reject the case.
- [minor] `Header().Set("ETag", "")` is treated as a handler-set ETag. The response then carries an empty `ETag:` header and no generated one. Reproduced: header values `[""]`. Arguably "sets an ETag" in the spec's sense, so it is a judgment call.
- [minor] `ifNoneMatch` drops the whole header line at the first malformed member, so `"a b", "c"` does not match `"c"`. Criterion 6 only requires malformed members to never match, so this is not a violation. Reproduced as a divergence from a lenient parser.
- [minor] A handler that calls `WriteHeader(200)` and then `WriteHeader(103)` gets the 103 forwarded immediately, ahead of the held 200. Reproduced: recorder code is 103. This is an unrealistic call order; net/http's own handling of this sequence was not compared.
- [minor] Reversed order `r.Use(Compress(5), ETag)` gives the identity ETag to gzip output. This is documented in the doc comment ("place ETag before it"), so it is not a defect.
CHECKS:
- (a) `r.Use(ETag, Compress(5))` over httptest.NewServer, Accept-Encoding gzip → pass: body decodes, gzip ETag is strong and differs from identity, `Vary: Accept-Encoding` kept, gzip ETag in If-None-Match → 304 with Content-Encoding removed. Cross-encoding If-None-Match with identity request → 200.
- (b) `GetHead,ETag` and `ETag,GetHead` → pass: GET and HEAD ETags equal, HEAD body empty, HEAD If-None-Match → 304, empty GET ETag = sha256("").
- (b) `Logger,Recoverer,ETag` → pass for GET (HEAD not routed, since the probe had no GetHead).
- (c) ServeContent plain 200 → pass (ETag present). Range → 206 with no ETag. If-Modified-Since current → 304 with no ETag. Old If-Modified-Since → 200. If-None-Match on the generated ETag → 304. Handler-set `W/"own"` with If-None-Match `"own"` → 304 and the header is kept.
- (d) io.Copy from a 2.4 MB *os.File, empty file, `ReadFrom(strings.Reader)`, and 7-byte writes → pass: all ETags match a whole-body SHA-256.
- Criterion 10 error wording: Hijack and Push with a non-capable writer → pass, exact compress.go text. Flush during buffered 200 → pass (Flushed false). 201 Flush → pass (Flushed true). POST Flush → pass (passthrough, no ETag).
- Criterion 9: 103 with Link forwarded before the 200, which carries the ETag → pass.
- Criterion 8: double WriteHeader(201) then 500 → pass (201 kept, body kept). Write then WriteHeader(404) → pass (implicit 200 wins, ETag set).
- Criterion 11: late X-B and late ETag not sent; X-A kept at the value set before WriteHeader → pass.
- Criterion 12: Recoverer outside ETag after a buffered write then panic → pass (500, no partial body, no ETag).
- Criterion 6 table (28 cases through ifNoneMatch): weak both ways, `"a","b"`, `,,"a",,`, prefix `"ab"` vs `"abc"`, case `"ABC"`, `abc`, unterminated, `W/abc`, empty and whitespace-only lines, `*` with and without a handler ETag, `"a"x,"b"`, tabs, `"a,b"`, UTF-8 → all pass except the `"a b", "c"` case noted above.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent requests through ETag+Compress under `-race` → pass.
- Hijack variants with `none`/`WriteHeader`/`Write` → only the two buffered variants fail (see the blocking finding).
OPEN QUESTIONS: Should Hijack after a buffered 200 send the held head (matching net/http) or refuse? The fix is the orchestrator's call. The criteria do not say.
